name: Fumio Okura
bio: [Fumio Okura](https://fokura.jp) is an Associate Professor at the University of Osaka (Japan). He received his M.Sc. and Ph.D. in engineering from the Nara Institute of Science and Technology in 2011 and 2014, respectively. His research lies at the intersection of computer vision and computer graphics, with recent work focusing on plant phenotyping. He has received several awards, including the IPSJ/IEEE Computer Society Young Computer Researcher Award.
talkTitle: Plant Phenotyping as a Frontier for Computer Vision
talkAbstract: Plant phenotyping (PP) poses a range of challenging computer vision (CV) problems, which cannot be fully addressed by simply applying existing CV techniques. In this talk, I will present several case studies from my own research experience, illustrating how problems arising from PP can be formulated as CV problems and developed into contributions to the CV community.

name: Susie Robinson
bio: [Susie Robinson](https://www.linkedin.com/in/susie-robinson-emphasis/) leads EMPHASIS, the pan-European Research Infrastructure for plant phenotyping, a globally significant network of distributed infrastructure, enabling services and expertise supporting research and innovation for new and improved crops, healthier food, more sustainable agricultural practice and development of novel plant-based bio-products. Susie also has strong interests and expertise in corporate governance, and has held prior senior and executive roles in the UK and South Australian Governments in the portfolios of innovation, research, higher education, treasury and finance, and public sector performance.
talkTitle: Building the Ecosystem: Research Infrastructures and Computer Vision for Plant Phenotyping
talkAbstract:
Drawing on experience developing plant phenotyping research infrastructures in Australia and Europe, this keynote will explore how distributed research infrastructures can support the development, testing, sharing and adoption of computer vision approaches. Using EMPHASIS as the example, I will consider how infrastructures can connect facilities, data, technologies, expertise and communities to turn innovation into shared and sustainable capability.

This relationship must be bi-directional: what can the computer vision community contribute, to strengthen research infrastructures? The talk will consider how sharing datasets, tools, workflows and expertise can help build an ecosystem in which infrastructure and innovation develop together.
